To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vitro mitochondrial complementation observed in Neurospora iv-requiring mutants is due to the secretion of dihydrourine (DHV), a precursor of valine, from mitochondria of the mutant strain 330A (iv-1) into the assay milieu where it is dehydrated by dehydratase purified form the soluble fraction of Neurospora to yield ketovaline.

the complementation of valine biosynthesis in Neurospora can be explained by the secretion of dihydric acid intermediates from the mitochondria into an extramitochondrial milieu, where the enzymes catalyzing the next two steps in the biosynthetic sequence (DHV to ketovaline and ketovaline to valine) reside.

(1) the in vitro mitochondrial complementation of the iv-1 mutation in strain 330A is due to the secretion of dihydroyvaline by mitochondria, and (2) two different mitochondrial populations can complement each other in vitro when the two populations are separated by a dialysis bag.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the in vivo and in vitro complementation of two iv-requiring Neurospora mutants for the biosynthesis and metabolism of valine.
the elucidation of the mechanism of mitochondrial complementation.
the elucidation of the mechanism whereby mitochondria from two different iv-requiring mutants can complement each other in vitro for the biosynthesis in the mitochondria of the amino acid, valine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the in vitro complementation of the iv-1 mutant 330a is mediated via the secretion and subsequent enzymatic conversion of DHV to ketovaline, and the latter metabolite is the actual substrate for the mitochondrial transamination reaction.
the in vitro complementation observed in this work is the result of the shunting of DHV and ketovaline across the mitochondrial membrane.
the in vitro complementation in the iv system is mediated by DHV and that this metabolite is the only substance that can be exchanged between the two populations of mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the complementation of valine synthesis in the Neurospora iv mutants is accomplished by the secretion of DHV from mitochondria, followed by its enzymatic transformation to ketovaline outside the organelles, with the latter diffusing back into mitochondria to be converted to valine by the transamination of alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase.
in vitro mitochondrial complementation for the biosynthesis and utilization of valine is mediated by an interorganellar shunt pathway.
mitochondrial complementation is mediated by a combination of enzymatic and diffusional mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial compartment is capable of exchanging metabolites with the cytoplasm.
the mitochondria of a eukaryotic cell are able to communicate with the cytoplasm, even when they are separated from it by a semipermeable barrier.

mitochondrial complementation can occur in vitro and in vivo in Neurospora and that the mechanism of complementation is via secretion of DHV and its conversion to ketovaline outside the mitochondria, followed by diffusion of the latter into mitochondria for transamination to val.
